info.title: Core System API
info.description: Enterprise Core System — capacités transverses (identity, ledger, wallet) exposées à plusieurs produits. Authentification par API key (`Authorization: Bearer pk_<env>_<id>.<secret>`), voir `GET /v1/whoami`.

get.description:
Resolves the bearer API key and returns which Project it belongs to,
in which environment (sandbox/live), and which scopes it carries. The
first call an integrating product should make to confirm its
credentials.

post.description:
Requires the `notifications:write` scope and an `Idempotency-Key`
header (spec §13). `to_party_ref` is a correlation reference only
— resolving it to an actual delivery address is a provider adapter
concern, not the Core's (ADR-0041 §5).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Caller-supplied unique key used for both the HTTP-level response cache and the use case's own duplicate-effect guard. Same key + same body = cached response, never a second effect. Same key + different body = 409. See ADR-0025 (idempotency design) and G7 (mandatory on every monetary mutation route).

post.description:
The request names only a `channel` (e.g. `mtn_momo`, `card`), never a
provider — `StartPaymentUseCase` resolves which adapter actually
handles it via the Project's routing configuration (ADR-0038 §2).
Requires the `payments:write` scope and an `Idempotency-Key` header
(G7, ADR-0025). Crediting a wallet on success is never implicit — it
only happens if `wallet_recipient_external_ref` is given (ADR-0037).
Prefer `POST /v1/payments/paylink` or `POST /v1/payments/payin`
for new integrations.

get.description:
Reads the Core's own last-known state only — no live call to the
provider. Requires the `payments:read` scope, and returns the same
not-found response whether the payment doesn't exist or belongs to
another project.

idempotency_key.description:
Review finding, user-directed: this is the documented
fallback truth source when a webhook is missed — it must
hand back the same caller-supplied context the webhook
already does (its own Idempotency-Key, and the callback_url
it registered), or polling here loses information the
webhook has.

PaymentFlow.description: Discriminates between the two payment initiation flows exposed by aggregator-style providers. `Payin` is the synchronous, app-driven flow (used by mobile apps and server-to-server integrations that drive the customer through their own UX). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /payin`; CinetPay exposes it as `POST /v2/payment`; MTN exposes it as `POST /collection/.../requesttopay`.  `Paylink` is the hosted-link, redirect-driven flow (used by web apps that hand the customer off to a provider-hosted page). MyCoolPay exposes this as `POST /paylink`; CinetPay returns a `payment_url` alongside the same initiation call (the discriminator is implicit).  Providers that do not distinguish the two flows (e.g. CinetPay) treat `Payin` as the default and ignore the discriminator on the `InitiatePaymentCommand`.
PaymentFlow.title: PaymentFlow

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/webhook-endpoints`. Authorization (the
`webhooks:write` scope) is checked in the controller against
`ProjectContext`, not here.

url.description:
`SafeOutboundUrlRule` (security review finding — this used
to accept any http(s) URL, including internal/private
targets: SSRF, and a persistent one at that, since a
registered endpoint is retried and DLQ-replayed).

RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest.title: RegisterWebhookEndpointRequest

StartPaymentRequest.description:
Validates `POST /v1/payments`. Authorization (the `payments:write`
scope) is checked in the controller against `ProjectContext`, not
here — this class only validates shape, never identity.

No `idempotency_key` body field: the `Idempotency-Key` HTTP header
(required by the `idempotency` middleware ahead of this request ever
reaching validation — ADR-0025, G7) is the one value used for both
the HTTP-level response cache and `StartPaymentUseCase`'s own
provider-call protection. One key, not two.
